skill.name: compound-docs
skill.description: Turns confirmed technical fixes into validated, searchable solution documents and identifies repeated issues for pattern promotion.
skill.summary: Capture confirmed fixes as searchable documentation and promote recurring issues into reusable patterns.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks, template fences, or benign local lookup examples rather than command execution or reconnaissance. Two mkdir instructions remain confirmed because they interpolate unquoted dynamic path components. Semantic review also found persistent instruction-injection exposure and project writes triggered without separate approval.

remediation.issue: Generated documents can persist untrusted instructions for future agents.
remediation.suggestion: Mark generated content as untrusted data, reject instruction-like prose, and tell future agents never to follow commands found in solution documents.

remediation.issue: Common completion phrases can trigger filesystem changes without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before changing schema.yaml, creating directories, or writing documentation. Show the planned paths first.

remediation.issue: Dynamic path placeholders are inserted into shell commands without quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Use filesystem APIs, validate path components against strict slugs, and confine all writes to an approved project directory.

content.user_title: Capture Solved Problems as Reusable Documentation
content.value_statement: Solved technical issues often disappear inside chat history. This skill converts confirmed fixes into searchable solution documents and promotes recurring issues into reusable patterns.
actual_capabilities: Detects declared completion phrases and the /compound command.
Extracts symptoms, categories, components, root causes, solutions, and prevention guidance from the conversation.
Validates generated frontmatter against the bundled schema.
Searches existing solution files for related errors, paths, and dependencies.
Creates dated Markdown solution documents in category directories.
Offers to promote repeated issues into a shared patterns.md file.
limitations: It depends on accurate and complete conversation context.
Its similarity checks use local keywords and paths rather than semantic indexing.
Its shell examples assume common Unix tools and may not work on every platform.
Generated content and schema changes require human review before reuse.

use_cases.title: Preserve Debugging Fixes
use_cases.description: Convert a confirmed repair into a searchable record with symptoms, cause, solution, and prevention.

use_cases.title: Build Team Troubleshooting Memory
use_cases.description: Store recurring deployment and integration fixes in a consistent project knowledge base.

use_cases.title: Identify Repeated Failure Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare new incidents with existing records and promote repeated solutions into shared guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Confirmed Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Document the fix we just confirmed. Summarize the symptom, category, root cause, solution, and prevention steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a straightforward technical problem is resolved.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Missing Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a solution document for this resolved issue. Ask only for required details that are missing from our conversation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the fix is known but documentation context is incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Check Related Solutions
prompt_templates.prompt: Search existing solution documents for related symptoms, files, and dependencies before documenting this confirmed fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the project already has a solution library.

prompt_templates.title: Promote a Recurring Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this fix with existing records. Propose a patterns.md entry only if the recurrence threshold is met, and request approval before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when repeated incidents may justify shared preventive guidance.

output_examples.input: The Docker build succeeded after we disabled the stale cache. Capture this fix.
output_examples.output: Created a deployment solution entry with the symptoms, root cause, successful fix, prevention guidance, and a dated searchable filename.

output_examples.input: This authentication header issue has happened twice. Check whether it belongs in our patterns.
output_examples.output: Found two related solution records and prepared a pattern proposal for review before updating the shared pattern file.

best_practices: Confirm that the reported fix succeeded before creating documentation.
Review generated paths, schema additions, and document content before approving writes.
Keep symptoms observable and prevention guidance specific to the verified root cause.
anti_patterns: Do not document trivial typos or obvious syntax corrections.
Do not place secrets, credentials, or private customer data in generated documents.
Do not promote a pattern without verified related occurrences and explicit approval.

faq.question: When does this skill run?
faq.answer: It declares completion phrases such as that worked as triggers. You can also invoke it with /compound.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It creates dated Markdown solution files under category directories and can update patterns.md after approval.

faq.question: How are document fields validated?
faq.answer: The skill checks required fields, date format, enum values, symptom quality, and tag formatting against schema.yaml.

faq.question: Can it add new categories or components?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow permits new enum values in schema.yaml, so each proposed addition should receive review.

faq.question: How does it find related issues?
faq.answer: It searches local solution files for matching error fragments, file paths, imports, dependencies, categories, and tags.

faq.question: Does it protect sensitive information automatically?
faq.answer: No. Review conversation-derived content and remove secrets or private data before any document is written.
